cards.gloss_en: a natural tendency to do something
cards.ex_en: He has a propensity for asking too many questions.

cards.gloss_en: to argue earnestly to warn or dissuade someone
cards.ex_en: She expostulated with him about his careless spending.
cards.ex_cn: 她苦口婆心劝他别乱花钱。

cards.gloss_en: the act of asking for something again and again
cards.ex_en: At last he gave in to her importunity and stayed.
cards.ex_cn: 最后他拗不过她的再三央求，留了下来。

cards.ex_en: He grew tired of their endless importunities for money.
cards.ex_cn: 他们没完没了地讨钱，他都烦了。

cards.ex_en: The children thought they saw an apparition in the hall.
cards.ex_cn: 孩子们以为在走廊里看到了鬼影。

cards.ex_en: A small stream ran betwixt the two hills.
cards.ex_cn: 一条小溪从两座山之间流过。

cards.gloss_en: deep sorrow for having done wrong
cards.ex_en: He knelt in penitence and asked to be forgiven.

cards.gloss_en: never getting tired even after long effort
cards.ex_en: The indefatigable nurse worked all day without a break.
cards.ex_cn: 这位不知疲倦的护士忙了一整天没歇过。

cards.gloss_en: units used to measure the depth of water
cards.ex_en: The anchor sank many fathoms to the seabed.
cards.ex_cn: 锚沉了好几英寻才到海底。

cards.gloss_en: a reduction in the strength or amount of something
cards.ex_en: We waited for the abatement of the storm before sailing.
cards.ex_cn: 我们等风暴平息后才启航。

cards.gloss_cn: 天意眷顾的、恰巧幸运的
cards.gloss_en: happening by lucky, seemingly heaven-sent chance
cards.ex_en: Their rescue was a providential turn of events.
cards.ex_cn: 他们获救真是天意的巧合。
